verses.text: No! [1] I swear by the Day of Resurrection.
And, no! I swear by the reproaching (inner) self.
Does man think that We will not reassemble his bones?
Yes indeed; We are Able to form his very fingertips.
Rather, man wants to commit vice ever onward.
He asks, “When is the Day of Resurrection?”
So, when the sight is dazzled [2],
and the moon is eclipsed,
and the sun and the moon are joined together—
man says on that day, “Where is the escape?”
But no! There is no refuge.
To your sg Lord on that day everything comes to reside.
Man is informed on that day of whatever he put forth and whatever he left behind.
Rather, man is an eyewitness against himself,
even as he presents his excuses.
Do not rush your sg tongue with it[3] to hurry on with it.
Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation.
So, when We have recited it, follow sg its recitation;
then upon Us is its explanation.
But no! Rather, you pl love the fleeting life
and you [4] leave aside the Hereafter.
Some faces on that day are radiant,
looking towards their Lord.
And some faces on that day are gloomy,
expecting that a back-breaking blow will be dealt them.
But no! Rather, when it[5] has reached the collarbone,
and it is said, “Who is the healer?”
And one realizes that it is the final departure,
and leg is entwined with leg[6] —
to your sg Lord on that day is the driving (of people).
Then, (as for) one who neither believed nor prayed,
but disbelieved and turned away,
then went to his family, strutting—
(this punishment is) more and more suitable for you sg.
Then again, more and more suitable for you.
Does man think that he will be left without purpose?
Was he not a drop of emitted semen [7]?
Then he became a clinging form, which He then created and formed?
And made of him the two spouses[8], the male and the female?
Is not that One able to revive the dead?

footnotes.1: Qira’at: Qunbol and Al-Bazzi in his second narration read it as: “Surely, I swear by…”
footnotes.2: Qira’at: Nafie’ and Abu Ja’far read it as: “So, when the sight glows…”
footnotes.4: Qira’at: Ibn Kathir, Abu ‘Amr, Ibn ‘Amer and Ya’qub read it as: “But no! Rather, they love the fleeting life 21 21 and they leave aside the Hereafter.”
footnotes.5: Referring to the soul as it leaves the body.
footnotes.6: Referring to the shrouding of the body after death, before burial.
footnotes.7: Qira’at: All except for Hafs and Ya’qub read it as: “Was he not an emitted drop of semen?”
footnotes.8: The Arabic word zawjayn can also mean ‘two kinds’ or ‘two types’.
